newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius bank rate up on tight monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius bank rate up on tight monetary policy.

text.p: The bank rate in Mauritius rose in July on monetary tightening by the central Bank of Mauritius to contain inflation, Bank of Mauritius said on Monday.
"(The bank rate) fluctuated between 9.31 percent and 9.48 percent in July 1996, as compared to a range of 9.07 to 9.45 percent in the previous month," the bank said in a report.
"Bank Rate picked up during the month of July 1996, signalling tighter monetary policy stance of the Bank of Mauritius to contain inflationary pressures," the report added.
In mid-August, the economic planning ministry revised the inflation rate for the financial year ending 30 June 1996 to 5.8 percent, up from an earlier forecast of 5.6 percent made in May.

The central bank said it put a total of 3.125 billion rupees ($154 million) of treasury bills on tender sale in July. It received bids totalling 3.2 billion rupees and sold a total 2.8 billion rupees worth of bills.
"Marked preference was noted for the short maturity bills during the month," the report said.

In June, the Bank of Mauritius sold 800 million rupees of treasury bills out of the same amount put on tender and received bids amounting 1.4 billion rupees. The central bank said the overall average weighted yield for the bills auctions in July increased to 9.13 percent from 8.96 percent in June.
In the foreign exchange market, the report said foreign exchange reserves of the central bank fell around 5.0 percent to 14.8 billion rupees in July from 15.6 billion rupees in June.

"The main feature in the local forex market, for the month of July, was the continuous appreciation of the dollar vis a vis the rupee. These reserves represent 21.4 weeks of imports on the value of import bill for the fiscal year 1995-96," it said.
The Mauritian rupee depreciated by 0.89 percent against the dollar between June and July 1996.
"Regarding the rupee/dollar rate, the weighted average interbank ask rate was at 20.3469 rupees, nearly 50 cents higher than that for the month of June," the report said.

The central bank sold a total of 29.6 million dollars in the interbank forex market during interventions while hard currency receipts for the bank from sugar export totalled 3.5 million dollars, it said.
